newsitem.title: USA: NRC sees Salem 2 nuke restart approval by weekend.
newsitem.headline: NRC sees Salem 2 nuke restart approval by weekend.

text.p: The Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Monday it will likely grant approval to restart the 1,106 megawatt (MW) Salem nuclear power unit 2 in southern New Jersey by this weekend.
"It could happen by the end of the week," an NRC spokesman replied when asked about a date when the regional NRC chief Hubert Miller will give the go-ahead.
Salem 2's restart has been stalled due to valve repairs discovered more than a week ago.
The unit's reactor reached "hot standby" status from "hot shutdown" over the weekend.
NRC officials are waiting for updates on the readiness of Salem 2 before giving clearance to startup.
"There's criticality testing through midweek," the NRC spokesman noted.
Salem 2 and the adjoining unit 1 with the same generating capacity have been shut for more than two years to address safety concerns raised by the NRC.
The Salem units are operated and partially owned by Public Service Electric & Gas Co. Other owners are Atlantic Energy Co, PECO Energy CO and Delmarva Power & Light Co
